identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal sözlükte kaydedilen varlık adını ve kaynakların etimolojik açıklamasını verir; güç, sahiplik veya egemenlik anlamı vermez.
identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, ilahi haberci varlığın tekil adını ve çoğul sınıfını doğrudan tanımlar; ayrıca adı haber götürme ve elçilik anlamıyla ilişkilendirilen daha eski biçimlerden açıklar. Dal, mevcut zarf içinde bu sözlük biçimi ve etimolojik açıklama olarak tutulabilir; güç, özel sahiplik ya da kamusal egemenlik anlamı sayılmamalıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Mekanik kapsam çözümlenmemiştir; hiçbir çıplak kök anlamı varsayılmaz ve kavram yalnız kaynakta açıklanan ad ile etimolojik tartışma düzeyinde tutulur.

baseline.text: De ki: O'nun dışında öne sürdüklerinize yalvarın. Onlar sizden zararı gidermeye de başka yöne çevirmeye de güç yetiremezler.

activation_trace.role: Uttered speech externalizes the challenge and makes the test public.
Calling draws the alleged agents into the attempted response relation that tests them.
A claim lacking secure warrant supplies the proposition put under test.
Ownership as effective disposal supplies the criterion that the attempted call fails.

changed_reading.after: The ayah stages an executable audit of a spoken claim: call the alleged agents, then judge the claim by their lack of disposal over harm.
changed_reading.before: The ayah simply states that beings besides God cannot help.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The sequence qal, invoke, those you claimed, then they do not possess turns an assertion into a test.
baseline_models.mechanism: A spoken claim about other agents is made operational: the addressees must call them, and the claim is measured against actual power of disposal over harm.

activation_trace.role: Lifting a cover also supplies the functional image of removing the affliction.
Loss, illness, and bad condition supply the burden on which both operations would have to act.
Change from one state or place to another supplies the second, distinct exit operation.
Capacity to maneuver or devise a way around a condition sharpens tahwil as rerouting, not mere motion.

changed_reading.after: The paired terms close two different escape routes: the alleged agents can neither terminate the harm nor alter its state, destination, or trajectory.
changed_reading.before: Kashf and tahwil are two near-synonyms for relief.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The coordinated negatives distinguish kashf al-durr from tahwil rather than repeating one incapacity.
baseline_models.mechanism: Kashf supplies lifting or removal, while tahwil supplies change of state or route. Together they deny both available exits from affliction: ending it here and moving or reconfiguring it elsewhere.

activation_trace.role: Proximity below or short of the goal supplies a graded station rather than a second endpoint.
Otherness and lower rank keep that proximate station distinct from the sovereign.
Sovereignty supplies the terminal capacity that rank or proximity does not confer.

changed_reading.after: The ayah can address revered or proximate subordinate figures while insisting that being near, high, or other-than is not sovereign command over harm.
changed_reading.before: Besides Him marks only a flat binary between God and false alternatives.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Min dunihi can activate a station that is other than, lower than, or near yet short of the endpoint.
baseline_models.mechanism: The called figures may occupy a proximate or subordinate station without possessing terminal sovereignty. The ayah separates nearness or rank from control.

activation_trace.role: The challenged human call supplies the relation whose efficacy is being tested.
The divine call supplies an initiating summons that the ayah immediately pairs with response.
Answering speech supplies achieved completion, contrasting with the failed capacity test in the focus.
The repeated invocation identifies the same class of called figures for the following dependency predicate.
Active seeking makes the called figures pursuers of access rather than sources of it.
Comparative nearness ranks the seekers while leaving the sought endpoint beyond them.

changed_reading.after: The context redraws the invocation as a dependency chain: those treated as endpoints are themselves seekers, while the effective call-response sequence belongs to the divine summons.
changed_reading.before: Calling the alleged agents merely demonstrates that they fail to answer.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context first presents a divine call immediately answered, then identifies the figures invoked in the focus and predicates seeking and nearness of them. The object of human invocation is therefore not an endpoint but a dependent seeker within the same relation.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies mirrored calling, an answered divine summons, and invoked figures who seek toward their Lord; I infer that the role reversal exposes nested dependence. A live alternative is that 17:52 concerns resurrection alone and does not generalize every call-response relation.
structural_cues: 17:52 orders the divine call immediately before human response.
17:57 identifies those invoked and then predicates seeking, relative nearness, hope, and fear of them.

activation_trace.role: A near but sub-terminal station supplies the location of the alleged intermediaries.
Maneuvering and seeking a workaround supply the shortcut that the negative closes.
Seeking directs even the hypothetical gods toward a destination beyond themselves.
An extended traversable path supplies the directional relation toward the throne.
Failure to attain a path supplies the contextual image of blocked routing.
The invoked figures' seeking confirms that they travel the route rather than control it.
Degrees of nearness supply ranked positions on the route without creating a rival endpoint.

changed_reading.after: It also denies the imagined shortcut itself: every proximate figure remains on a route toward the sovereign and therefore cannot route harm around that sovereign.
changed_reading.before: The ayah denies that another power can redirect a discrete harmful event.

context_deltas.mechanism: Repeated seeking, path, inability to find a path, means, and relative nearness turn the focus into route geometry. Figures short of the goal cannot furnish a tahwil that bypasses the endpoint toward which they themselves travel.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a repeated route lexicon and the focus branch of dun as near yet short of the goal; I infer that tahwil cannot function as a sovereign bypass. The materially live alternative is ordinary other-than for dun and concrete relocation for tahwil.
structural_cues: 17:42 makes hypothetical plural gods seek a path toward the possessor of the throne.
17:48 denies the opponents a path, while 17:57 makes the invoked figures seek the branchless wasilah and asks which is nearer.

activation_trace.role: Strength and cohesion supply the material command that the invoked figures lack.
State-to-state change lets tahwil receive the surrounding material transformation sequence.
Fragmentation supplies the maximally disintegrated starting state.
Creative bringing-into-being supplies the counter-operation to disintegration.
Iron hardness supplies an imagined resistant state that still falls within transformative command.
Return after departure supplies reversal of the apparently terminal state.
Origination supplies the agency criterion for who can effect the return.

changed_reading.after: In the resurrection sequence it can also expose the invoked figures' inability to convert the underlying state itself; transformative command belongs with origination and return.
changed_reading.before: Tahwil means only transferring affliction to another location or recipient.

context_deltas.mechanism: The preceding sequence moves through pulverized remains, new creation, imagined iron hardness, return, and first origination. This expands tahwil from relocating harm to commanding the material state that constitutes or reverses the condition.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies disintegration, resistant materials, return, and origination; I infer that the agent who initiates and reverses those states is the relevant possessor of tahwil. A live narrower reading limits tahwil to moving harm between persons or places.
structural_cues: 17:49-51 forms a progression from bones and fragments through stone or iron to return by the one who originated the addressees.
17:52 completes that progression with a call followed by embodied response.

activation_trace.role: Lifting a cover anchors the added reading of relief as removal of occlusion.
Bad condition and loss allow perceptual blockage to function as one form of harm without exhausting the noun.
A screening barrier supplies the first explicit layer of occlusion.
Covering makes the barrier itself hidden and sharpens the inverse relation to kashf.
A preserving cover placed over the hearts supplies an inward layer of blockage.
Weight in the ear supplies sensory obstruction rather than simple absence of information.
Failure of understanding supplies the functional consequence of the layered covers.

changed_reading.after: It can additionally include removal of the hidden condition that blocks perception and understanding; the alleged agents cannot peel away those layers.
changed_reading.before: Kashf al-durr denotes relief from an externally imposed hardship.

context_deltas.mechanism: The earlier context layers a hidden veil, protective coverings, and weight in the ears until understanding fails. Against that field, kashf al-durr can carry an epistemic layer: removal of an occluding condition, not only relief from an external event.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies multiple occluding layers and failed understanding; I infer that the focus's kashf branch can absorb this as one species of removing harm. The live alternative is that durr remains wholly general or bodily and that the veil sequence is only analogical.
structural_cues: 17:45 calls the veil itself hidden, creating a cover whose operation is not directly seen.
17:46 coordinates covers over hearts, weight in ears, failed understanding, and turning away.

activation_trace.role: Effective ownership supplies the authority denied without denying every status of the called figures.
An agent who sufficiently keeps an affair supplies the comprehensive office explicitly withheld from the messenger.
Degree and excellence preserve real rank while distinguishing it from ownership.
Prophetic reporting from God supplies an honored dependent office rather than autonomous disposal.

changed_reading.after: The context lets the ayah preserve authentic rank, prophecy, and gift while sharply denying that such honor entails delegated ownership over relief or transfer.
changed_reading.before: The incapacity statement lowers or dismisses the beings whom people invoke.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediate context denies comprehensive guardianship to the messenger, then affirms differentiated prophetic rank and gift. This separates genuine honor and office from delegated sovereign disposal, clarifying what the focus negates.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a denied guardianship office beside affirmed prophetic rank and gift; I infer a deliberate boundary between honor and sovereign disposal. A live alternative is that 17:54 limits only the messenger's coercive responsibility and does not classify every invoked figure.
structural_cues: 17:54 denies that the messenger was sent as wakil over the addressees.
17:55 immediately affirms differences of prophetic rank and a specific scriptural gift before 17:56 denies ownership to invoked figures.

remaining_uncertainties: Dun may function only as ordinary other-than rather than activating graded proximity.
Tahwil may remain narrower than ontological transformation despite the resurrection sequence.
The veil model may be analogical rather than a direct species of durr.
The surety and ledger model should remain exploratory and non-literal.
strongest_changes: 17:57 turns the invoked figures into dependent seekers rather than endpoints of invocation.
The path and nearness sequence makes min dunihi a possible sub-terminal station and closes the imagined sovereign shortcut.
The resurrection sequence expands tahwil from relocation into command over material state, return, and re-creation.
The veil sequence lets kashf al-durr include removal of an occluding condition without reducing durr to that layer.
summary.what_was_special: The packet's repeated call and route structures produced the strongest revisions, while the M-L-K angel/ownership branch collision and the surety-transfer cluster preserved two unusually concrete but containable readings.

activation_trace.role: The angel branch supplies a salient class of exalted beings previously made objects of false attribution.
The possession branch supplies the capacity explicitly denied to such invoked beings.
Unwarranted attribution links the earlier claim about angels to the focus's challenged claims.

changed_reading.after: The packet permits a controlled M-L-K branch switch: malaikah are named, then yamlikun denies mulk, severing exalted identity from possessive power.
changed_reading.before: Exalted beings are mentioned in one passage, and unrelated agents later fail to possess relief.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it depends on two branches of the same mapped M-L-K inventory rather than on ordinary syntax. It remains anchored by the exact angel occurrence in 17:40 and the possession verb in 17:56; downstream prose should call it a contextual lexical echo, not claim that angel and ownership are one lexical sense.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus negates yamlikun, while 17:40 has already named malaikah through another branch of the packet's same M-L-K inventory.

activation_trace.role: Surety and guarantee recast the claimed figures as alleged underwriters of the burden.
Title and disposal supply the authority needed to discharge or reassign the burden.
Compulsion and necessity supply the binding burden for the legal analogy.
Assignment of a debt to another supplies the precise juridical image of forbidden transfer.
Entrusting an affair to another supplies the agency relation that the context explicitly limits.
A written determination that establishes judgment supplies the fixed order against which reassignment is imagined.
The written line makes that determination ledger-like and materially stabilizes the analogy.

changed_reading.after: As a contained legal image, the invocation treats them as alleged guarantors who possess neither title to discharge the burden nor authority to novate or assign it against the written determination.
changed_reading.before: The invoked figures cannot redirect a harmful event.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it assembles legal branches of zam, mulk, and hawl into a surety-and-assignment analogy. It remains anchored in the focus's alleged guarantee, disposition, harm, and tahwil, and is sharpened by the denied wakil and written determination; downstream prose should present it as a juridical image, not as a claim that the ayah literally discusses debt law.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Zam can name surety, mulk effective title, and tahwil assignment of a debt to another party.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Claimed intermediaries lack both removal and rerouting capacity.** `ز ع م:B001/B003` is uncertain claim or surety, `م ل ك:B002` ownership/disposal, `ك ش ف:B001/B002` uncovers, `ض ر ر:B001/B005` harm and constrained edge, and `ح و ل:B001` changes state. The test asks not whether they are named but whether they can uncover or redirect harm. I infer practical incapacity falsifies claimed surety. Invocation is evaluated by causal control.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 17:67 enacts the test: in pressing harm the supposed objects disappear, proving they cannot remove or reroute the condition for which they were invoked.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **The false intermediary fails both removal and rerouting tests.** Lexical evidence: `م ل ك B002` (ownership and disposal) in `يَمْلِكُونَ`, `ك ش ف B001` (removing a cover from a thing) in `كَشْفَ`, `ض ر ر B001` (harm, loss, and adverse condition) in `ٱلضُّرِّ`, and `ح و ل B001` (turning or changing a thing from its state) in `تَحْوِيلًا`. Structural cue: 17:54 denies custodial authority to the messenger, 17:55 locates prophetic preference under divine knowledge, and 17:57 says the invoked figures themselves seek means and nearness. Assigned role: ownership would authorize intervention; disclosure would lift harm, and transformation would reroute it. Abductive move: the packet negates both capacities; I infer that an intermediary unable either to remove or convert the condition cannot be ultimate custodian. Reading change: the challenge is operational rather than merely titular, testing alleged powers against two concrete modes of relief.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 17:57 was decisive: the invoked figures' own search for means and comparative nearness confirms operational dependence more strongly than the bare negation of their power in 17:56.

words.gloss_range: commanded saying, declaration, and public articulation; the local imperative frames the whole following challenge
words.prose: {{ar:قُلِ}} ({{tr:quli}}) opens the ayah as commissioned speech: the Prophet is the implied singular addressee, and the whole challenge that follows is to be voiced through him. The word is not neutral narration; it performs the confrontation by making the false invocation test public. Its liaison into {{ar:ٱدْعُوا۟}} ({{tr:udʿū}}) keeps the two imperatives audibly joined, while same-surah and formula rows keep it inside a recurring speech-frame for exposing claims made besides God.
words.root_gloss_range: speech and saying, with local force narrowed to commanded proclamation

topics.headline: commissioned speech frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the ayah as a commanded utterance carried through the Prophet, not as an unattached argument.
topics.reason: QAC marks a 2ms imperative, and attachment evidence makes the following material the quoted complement of the opening speech command.

topics.headline: saying as confrontation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the act of saying is itself the public mechanism by which the claim is tested.
topics.reason: The q-w-l speech field fits the local imperative and is realized as a public declaration that launches the test.

topics.headline: joined imperatives and formula thread
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the first command flow into the second while keeping the recitational vowel from becoming a new semantic claim.
topics.reason: The liaison and variant rows are valid for sound and recitation pressure, but QAC and local syntax keep the semantic force at the level of joined command framing.

topics.headline: recurring directive thread
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees this opening as one instance of a recurring directive-speech thread now turned toward polemical exposure.
topics.reason: The same-surah and synthesis rows describe a coherent discourse role for the opening command without overriding the local imperative parse.

words.gloss_range: call, invoke, summon, or supplicate; locally narrowed to a challenge to invoke claimed intermediaries
words.prose: {{ar:ٱدْعُوا۟}} ({{tr:udʿū}}) turns the audience into participants in the test: the plural imperative tells them to invoke the very beings they claimed. The call-range is narrowed by the object phrase, so this is not permission but challenge; the result clause immediately exposes failure. Its forensic background makes the call feel like a summons to produce evidence, while challenge-formula parallels such as 34:22 and 35:13 and the same imperative later aimed at God in 17:110 create a contrast between futile and valid address. The failed invocation also anticipates the distress scene in 17:67, where false objects of call vanish from attention.
words.root_gloss_range: calling, summoning, inviting, supplication, and claim-language; local object and result clause select futile invocation as test

topics.headline: plural test command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the addressees ordered to stage the very invocation whose failure will expose them.
topics.reason: QAC marks a 2mp imperative with the relative pronoun as object, and the result clause makes the command a test scene.

topics.headline: call range narrowed by object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader keeps the broad call-and-prayer range in view while recognizing that the local object selects invocation of claimed intermediaries.
topics.reason: The d-ʿ-w range is real, but the relative object and besides-Him phrase narrow the local use to invoked intermediaries rather than ordinary calling.

topics.headline: imperative as challenge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader does not mistake the command for approval, because the ayah uses the command to generate the proof of incapacity.
topics.reason: The immediate negative result makes the command a challenge, and the claim or lawsuit image strengthens the evidentiary force without changing the grammar.

topics.headline: formulaic invocation contrast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the command as part of a wider refutation formula and as a same-surah contrast with valid calling to God (17:110).
topics.reason: The inter-ayah rows provide concrete formula references and same-surah contrast while the local parse remains governed by the imperative and its object.

topics.headline: later distress confirmation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees this challenge anticipate the later scene where distress exposes the disappearance of false objects of call (17:67).
topics.reason: The boundary and echo rows fit the ayah's movement from divine knowledge to direct challenge and its later same-surah confirmation.

words.gloss_range: definite masculine plural relative pronoun, locally the object of the invocation command and opener of the claim clause
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلَّذِينَ}} ({{tr:alladhīna}}) introduces the invoked group without granting them a title. As the object of {{ar:ٱدْعُوا۟}} ({{tr:udʿū}}), it delays identification until the claim clause arrives, making the group depend textually on what the addressees alleged. Its rational plural form lets the later plural verb test them as supposed agents, while the next ayah can then specify that these invoked ones themselves seek nearness.

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: preceding invocation command that takes the relative pronoun as object

topics.headline: object relative pronoun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the called objects introduced by grammar before they are defined by the claim against them.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify the relative pronoun as the direct object of the invocation command.

topics.headline: identity delayed by claim
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah withholds an honorific label and lets the addressees' own claim define the group.
topics.reason: The relative construction is completed by the claim verb, so the referent is textually dependent on the claim rather than on an independent noun.

topics.headline: claimed agents separated from claimants
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can distinguish the you-claimants from the they-claimed agents whose power is tested.
topics.reason: The masculine plural relative pronoun and later plural verb create a tested agent slot distinct from the second-person claimants.

topics.headline: referent opened for continuation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader is prepared for the next ayah to identify the invoked group more precisely rather than treating this word as the final description.
topics.reason: The boundary row coheres with the relative-pronoun openness and the continuation in 17:57.

words.gloss_range: you claimed or alleged; locally a completed, suspicious assertion by the addressed group
words.prose: {{ar:زَعَمْتُم}} ({{tr:zaʿamtum}}) pins the false premise to the addressed group: they have already made the claim, and the ayah now tests it. The verb is not neutral reporting; its allegation range and guarantor background make the claim sound unauthorized before the power verdict arrives. Its omitted predicate compresses the reductio, so the claim's alleged status is left unstated and then collapsed by the denial of possession. The exposure pattern also recalls claim-testing scenes such as 6:94, 18:48, 34:22, and the same-surah overreach at 17:92.
words.root_gloss_range: claiming, allegation, representation, and guarantor/spokesman associations; local form selects a completed second-person claim

topics.headline: completed claim by addressees
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the claim as already made by the very people now being challenged.
topics.reason: QAC marks a 2mp perfect with the addressees embedded in the suffix, making the claim a completed premise under test.

topics.headline: allegation not neutral report
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the claim prejudged as doubtful and unauthorized before the explicit incapacity verdict.
topics.reason: The lexical evidence supports allegation and doubtful assertion, while the guarantor image adds social pressure without replacing the local verb sense.

topics.headline: compressed claim predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah does not dignify the alleged status by naming it; it infers and defeats it through incapacity.
topics.reason: The relative object is present while the second predicate is recoverable, so the ayah compresses the premise and lets the negative result refute it.

topics.headline: claims tested by exposure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader locates this claim inside a recurring pattern where assertions meet disclosure and proof-failure, including 6:94, 18:48, 34:22, and 17:92.
topics.reason: The occurrence and co-occurrence rows give concrete references where claim language is tested, without overriding the local completed-claim grammar.

words.gloss_range: preposition forming the compound besides-Him phrase; locally supplies separation and exclusion
words.prose: {{ar:مِّن}} ({{tr:min}}) is small but decisive because it governs {{ar:دُونِهِۦ}} ({{tr:dūnihī}}) and helps form the exclusion phrase. It places the claimed beings in a domain apart from Him before the verdict of incapacity is stated. After the elevation language of 17:55, the phrase also turns the movement toward a lower, excluded realm without making the particle independently spatial.

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: following genitive complement in the besides-Him phrase

topics.headline: compound exclusion phrase
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the preposition actively helping construct the besides-Him exclusion, not merely filling space before the noun.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence show the preposition governing the following noun and forming the local compound phrase.

topics.headline: exclusion before incapacity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the claimed beings are positioned outside the divine referent before their lack of power is predicated.
topics.reason: The prepositional phrase belongs inside the claim object before the result clause, so scope and verdict are sequenced.

topics.headline: separation and hierarchy color
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the shift from prior elevation to the lower excluded domain, while the local grammar keeps the force tied to the compound phrase.
topics.reason: The hierarchy image survives as discourse color from the compound and boundary rows, but the particle itself remains a governed preposition rather than a standalone theological noun.

words.gloss_range: below, apart from, besides, short of; locally the genitive complement in the exclusion phrase with suffix referring to God
words.prose: {{ar:دُونِهِۦ}} ({{tr:dūnihī}}) gives the exclusion phrase its weight: the invoked beings are not merely different, but placed below and apart from Him. The attached suffix fixes the divine referent, while the root-image of below-ness and barrier turns besides-ness into a ranked and blocked relation. Same-surah rows keep this as part of a rejected-support arc from 17:2 through 17:97, but the local grammar makes it the claim-domain measured by the coming possession denial.
words.root_gloss_range: spatial below-ness, separation, barrier, and besides-ness; local construction selects excluded rival-domain relation

topics.headline: suffix fixes divine referent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the excluded domain defined in relation to God, not as a vague outside category.
topics.reason: QAC marks the noun with a third-person masculine suffix referring to God, and the prepositional attachment fixes its local role.

topics.headline: besides as below and barred
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels besides-ness as a lower and blocked relation rather than a neutral alternative location.
